method: Stage 1 citation-grounded + full-text recovery pass over mechanisms RQ5 recorded as never-defended. Two candidate generators were run: (a) citation-based - defense papers citing the paper that introduced an uncovered mechanism (147 candidates); (b) full-text - the mechanism's name appearing in a defense paper's body text with the bibliography stripped (35 candidates). Every candidate was adjudicated by reading the surrounding text. Bar: 'evaluated' only, per the project's precision-first standard; 'claimed' and 'related-work-only' are recorded but do NOT count as coverage.

method_findings.citation_control_recall: Citation matching re-found only 19 of 67 (28%) known-covered mechanisms, so it is a complementary signal, not a superset - defense papers routinely evaluate an attack via a bundled benchmark (AgentDojo, InjecAgent) without citing the original attack paper.
method_findings.dominant_pattern: Of 147 citation candidates, the overwhelming majority mention the mechanism only in the bibliography or a related-work sentence. Defense papers cite attack papers as related work, not as evaluation targets - which is direct evidence for RQ7's invention-outpaces-evaluation finding rather than a measurement artifact explaining it away.
method_findings.permanent_floor: 20 of the 116 uncovered mechanisms are UNNAMED (a descriptive label assigned during extraction, never a term the literature uses), so they cannot be recovered by any name-based search. This is a hard floor on what this method can measure.
